verbatim_v3_text: In March 2020, former Google engineer Anthony Levandowski faced a civil judgment exceeding one hundred seventy-nine million dollars. Hours later, he filed for bankruptcy. Uber had agreed to buy his startup and signed a conditional indemnification agreement covering certain legal risks. The judgment was personal, not a verdict against Uber. Could that agreement make Uber help pay?

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: Four years earlier, Levandowski had copied roughly fourteen thousand files from Google's internal self-driving project. He then started a company Uber would acquire. That transaction produced allegations of stolen technology, a fierce trial, and a separate settlement involving Uber shares worth roughly two hundred forty-five million dollars.
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. ~14k copied at Google and later Waymo-Uber trial; ~245m stock-value figure attributed to 2018 settlement, not theft verdict.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: But the stock settlement did not end every dispute tied to the acquisition. In 2022, Uber made another payment directly to Google under a different agreement. Court records establish that payment happened. They do not disclose how much Uber paid. To understand why it happened, start with the files.

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: At Google, Levandowski had been close to the engineering at the center of the self-driving race. He worked on an autonomous vehicle project that helped develop laser-based sensing, known as LiDAR. A system like that gives a vehicle information about the world around it. And the research behind it can be commercially valuable.
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Google-era autonomous vehicle/LiDAR role and sensing description; no allegation of proven misappropriation.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: To a rival building its own autonomous car, the people who understood these systems were valuable. To Google, however, there was another asset: confidential designs, documents, and information developed inside the company. You can hire an experienced engineer. That does not automatically give you the right to keep copies of the engineer's former employer's files.
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Employee expertise vs confidential employer materials correctly kept distinct; normative access principle no invented ruling.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: In December 2015, Google engineer Anthony Levandowski downloaded roughly fourteen thousand files from the company's internal self-driving project. Justice Department records say he moved the collection to a personal computer. That documents the copying. It does not establish that Uber later received or used all those files.

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: Levandowski left Google in January 2016. By then, a new business was taking shape. It was called Otto, and it was pursuing autonomous trucking. There was a practical business idea here: take expertise developed around self-driving cars and apply it to the much larger, heavier machines moving freight across America.
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Google exit January 2016, Otto autonomous-trucking venture and timing; commercial pivot presented as context.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: Google's concern would grow from what Levandowski did with confidential information while still under obligations to his former employer. acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: Uber was not simply calling a former Google employee about a job. In February 2016, Uber and Otto had a preliminary acquisition term sheet. independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Feb 2016 preliminary term sheet, April agreement and separate conditional indemnity; avoids saying deal already closed in April.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: That last arrangement deserves attention. Indemnification, in ordinary language, is an agreement about who may bear certain legal costs or liabilities. It is not a universal promise to pay whatever someone owes for any reason. The conditions and exclusions matter. In this story, their meaning would become contested years after the startup deal.

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

That headline number was not six hundred eighty million dollars wired to Levandowski.
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Up-to ~$680m acquisition headline contrasted with $100k initial cash and conditional equity; no false cash transfer.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: Think about what was being purchased: a young startup, a team, and the possibility of future performance. Uber was making a bet on what these people might build. acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

Its scope would be argued in another court, years later.

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Stroz forensic engagement occurs before acquisition completion; consistent with Delaware record.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

It does not establish, simply by describing those terms, that directors expected a particular crime or personally knew the contents of every retained document. The real business tension is narrower: how does a company price risk it cannot fully resolve before closing?

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: There was no tidy answer. Uber completed the Otto acquisition, and Levandowski took a senior role in its self-driving program. acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: In December 2016, a supplier accidentally sent Google an email meant for Uber, containing circuit-board drawings for autonomous-vehicle technology. According to the later court account, the drawings allegedly resembled Google's own engineering designs. That alleged similarity raised questions about Uber's LiDAR work; the email alone did not prove that Uber had used Google's confidential files.
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Supplier error December 2016; resemblance expressly alleged, not independently proven Uber use.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

But it gave Google a concrete reason to investigate a troubling possibility: had confidential work from its own self-driving project crossed into the rival program?
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Email is not 14k-file disclosure and not proof of theft; suspicion described as an open question.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: Waymo, the company created around Google's autonomous-driving project, filed a federal lawsuit in February 2017 against Uber and related Otto entities. It alleged misappropriation of trade secrets, including information about LiDAR, and pursued related claims. Those were allegations made in a complaint, not facts that a jury had already established.
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Feb 2017 complaint and its trade-secret allegations correctly separated from trial findings.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Uber denial and CEO regret attributed as positions, not admissions of secret use.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Two parties' competing evidentiary theories differentiated; no final verdict asserted.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

It treated the evidence that Levandowski had downloaded large quantities of confidential Google material as compelling. It raised serious questions about some LiDAR information and Uber. That was enough for specified interim restrictions while the lawsuit continued.

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

According to Uber, he later reported destroying them, and Uber said it never received the disks. Uber's delayed disclosure to Waymo became an evidentiary dispute.
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. March 2016 disks report is Uber's account; destruction qualified as reported and no confirmed transfer.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

He said jurors could draw an unfavorable inference, but were not required to. Uber said it never received the disks; their contents remained unverified. The case settled before a verdict.

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

What had been transferred? What had been used? What should a buyer have known? And would the jury ever get the opportunity to answer all of them?
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Rhetorical court questions properly framed as unresolved, not fabricated factual proof.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Trial opened first week Feb 2018; settlement before jury damages decision.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. ~245m contemporary value of shares, not cash criminal fine or damages verdict.
acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

And Uber's earlier Otto acquisition would bring a contested indemnification agreement back into focus.

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

acceptance_criterion: G04 V3 TEXT PASS; stage16 prepublication freshness remains required

verbatim_v3_text: What began with access to Google's confidential engineering files became a problem of ownership, evidence, contracts, and responsibility. Uber could buy a startup. It could hire people with extraordinary experience. But buying their future work did not automatically buy the right to their former employer's protected information—or erase the risks of what happened before the acquisition.
independent_finding: Rechecked V3 verbatim; unchanged from V2 paragraph with previous G04 V2 PASS. Editorial conclusion separates expertise purchase from Google confidentiality obligations; not accused-as-convicted.

It was a risk written into a deal—and argued about long after the deal closed.
